resources.string: Your toothbrush. No account. No phone number. No \"we value your privacy\".
No verification code required. Shocking, we know.
Pick it up – it\'s shy and naps a lot. Also close any other app that might be hogging it.
Negotiating. Unlike some apps, we\'re not asking for your date of birth.
Connected. Waiting for the brush to say something…
No brush found. Either it\'s asleep, or it ran off to sign up for a newsletter.
Wake it up (pick it up or tap the button) and try again.
Your brush fell asleep. Unlike certain apps, it doesn\'t phone home while sleeping.
Bluetooth is off. We\'re good, but not \"brush via telepathy\" good.
This device has no Bluetooth LE. Have you considered a manual toothbrush?
Connected to %1$s, but it doesn\'t speak the language we expected.
Android wants us to ask before using Bluetooth. Fair enough. That\'s all we ask for: no contacts, no location history, no blood type.
Your Android version insists on \"location\" to scan for Bluetooth devices. We don\'t even know what GPS is – this app has no internet permission, so where would we send it?
Permission denied. Respect. But without Bluetooth, this is just a very pretty screen.
Internet permission: none · Accounts created: 0 · Data sold: also 0
Not affiliated with Laifen, Philips or Oral-B. All trademarks belong to their owners. Made by someone who just wanted to brush his teeth.
Saved. On the brush. Not in some cloud. Imagine that.
The brush ignored that. At least it didn\'t ask for your e-mail.
Connection lost – the brush probably dozed off. Wake it, reconnect, save again. Your change is still here.
Invalid value. This should never happen – please report it.
Unsaved changes are kept until you reconnect.
Dentists say two minutes. The cloud has no opinion, because nobody asked it.
Stays on this phone. Copy it if you want to report a problem – we couldn\'t send it anywhere even if we wanted to.
A short buzz every 30 s to switch zones. Like a coach, minus the subscription.
Unlocks mode 4, the strongest vibration (strength 11–20). Without it, the button skips mode 4.
Only switchable on the brush. Bürstli doesn\'t dare touch it yet.
Only available while high frequency is on.
Remote control for your toothbrush. Because we can.
Bürstli can\'t control this toothbrush yet. You can help change that – no tech skills needed.

Here's how:
1. Take the brush off its charger.
2. Switch it on, as if you were brushing.
3. Put the phone next to it and wait about a minute.

Bürstli only listens. Nothing on the brush is changed.
Almost done… keep the brush running.
Recording… as long as you like.
Running for %1$d:%2$02d · stops by itself after 10 min
For nerds: record until I stop (max. 10 min)
If your phone asks whether to pair: tap “Pair”.
Now just send the report, for example by messenger or e-mail to whoever recommended Bürstli to you, or on GitHub. The device address and serial number have been removed.
Not everything worked, but half a report helps, too.
The report is copied – just paste it into the form.
Experimental: built from other people\'s research, not yet tried with Bürstli. Bürstli only reads, it changes nothing. If something looks wrong, a report helps a lot.
Record a report for this brush
Bürstli only listens to what this brush broadcasts, without connecting. It doesn\'t broadcast its battery level.
Shown only – Bürstli doesn\'t change this yet.
Switch your brush on and hold it close to the phone – it is usually at the top. The list shows Bluetooth devices nearby; it stays on this phone and only the one you pick goes into a report.
